【参考范文 · 170 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
To increase the likelihood of success, one should set realistic goals and work persistently towards them. This statement reveals a simple truth: ambition alone means little unless it is anchored to attainable targets and sustained effort.
A realistic goal keeps us moving instead of despairing. If a beginner runner vows to finish a marathon next week, failure is almost certain, and disappointment soon kills motivation. However, by aiming first at three kilometres, then five, and finally the full distance, the runner sets goals within reach and steadily raises the bar. Each small victory fuels the next.
Yet reasonable goals mean nothing without persistence. My cousin, who dreamed of passing CET-6, did not expect overnight fluency. She fixed a modest daily plan of thirty new words and one reading passage, and she stuck to it for months. As a result, she cleared the exam comfortably.
In this way, pairing sensible targets with steady work transforms a distant dream into a series of achievable steps. That is the surest road to success.

lines.en: M: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months. Your report is mostly good. But there are a couple of issues we must discuss. The report is yours to take with you. We'll go through the main points together now. And you can come through it in greater detail later. Do you have any questions before we start?
lines.zh: M: 好吧，这份是你的年度绩效评估。你已经在公司工作三年了，过去十二个月一直由我直接负责。你的报告总体不错，但有几个问题我们必须讨论一下。这份报告你可以带走。现在我们先一起过一遍重点，之后你可以再仔细看看。开始之前，你有什么问题吗？

lines.en: W: No, sir.
lines.zh: W: 没有，先生。

lines.en: M: I'll get straight to it then. It is evident that you are a hard worker. You are punctual and industrious. Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail. The company, myself included, is happy with your productivity and overall performance.
lines.zh: M: 那我就直说了。很明显，你工作很努力。你很守时，也很勤奋。此外，你有很强的分析能力，而且注重细节。公司，包括我在内，都对你的工作效率和整体表现感到满意。

lines.en: W: Thank you. I appreciate the recognition.
lines.zh: W: 谢谢。能得到这样的认可，我很感谢。

lines.en: M: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?
lines.zh: M: 那么，到目前为止，你同意这份描述吗？

lines.en: W: Yeah, it's a little simplistic perhaps. But that's to be expected from this kind of evaluation.
lines.zh: W: 嗯，也许有点过于简单了。不过，这种评估大概就是这样。

lines.en: M: Sure. Would you want to add anything? Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.
lines.zh: M: 当然。你想补充些什么吗？如果你愿意，我们可以把你的意见加到报告里。

lines.en: W: Oh, there's no need. It's a flattering portrayal really. Thank you, though.
lines.zh: W: 哦，没必要。说真的，这份描述已经很恭维我了。不过还是谢谢你。

lines.en: M: OK. This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others.
lines.zh: M: 好。这就说到不太好的部分了。主要涉及一个行为方面的问题，也就是你与他人合作的能力。

lines.en: W: I see.
lines.zh: W: 我明白了。

lines.en: M: Yes. As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.
lines.zh: M: 是的。你也知道，过去几个月里，有人对你的沟通方式提出了一些投诉。

lines.en: W: Of course, we already had like three meetings about this. Look, all I'm going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone. Simply put, I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago. And I already apologized if anyone was offended. But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.
lines.zh: W: 当然了，我们已经为这件事开过大概三次会了。听着，我只想说，我从来没打算冒犯任何人。简单来说，我不喜欢写很长的邮件，因为坦白说，我觉得那是在浪费时间。简洁就是效率。我觉得写长邮件会损害你刚才还在称赞的那种工作效率。如果有人觉得受到了冒犯，我也已经道过歉了。但说句完全坦诚的话，我认为那些感到被冒犯的人有点太敏感了。

lines.en: M: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?
lines.zh: M：那么请告诉我，你为什么想学医？

lines.en: W: I've always wanted to be a doctor. I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best. And I think that had a profound effect on me. As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!
lines.zh: W：我一直都想成为一名医生。我来自一个医疗条件始终不太好的小镇。我觉得这对我产生了深远的影响。小时候，我记得自己常常想，要是能服务社区、治愈病人，那该多好啊！

lines.en: M: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?
lines.zh: M：你生活中的其他哪些人或哪些事情促使你产生了成为医生的兴趣？

lines.en: W: Well, that's hard to say. I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard. And I certainly wouldn't be here without their support. I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me. At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.
lines.zh: W：这个很难说。我当然会说，我的父母是一个关键因素。他们总是督促我努力学习。要不是他们的支持，我肯定不会坐在这里。我想，我也非常幸运，身边有优秀的老师和朋友。总的来说，我一直处在一个积极向上的环境中，这个环境促使我努力学习、追逐梦想。

lines.en: M: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?
lines.zh: M：你有没有想专攻的医学分支？

lines.en: W: I haven't decided yet. It's still early days. However, if I had to say, internal medicine.
lines.zh: W：我还没决定。现在还早。不过，如果一定要说的话，我想选内科。

lines.en: M: Why internal medicine?
lines.zh: M：为什么是内科？

lines.en: W: I know it's no picnic. But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.
lines.zh: W：我知道这可不是件轻松的事。但我觉得内科最有意思，因为它涉及的范围很广，还把许多其他专科联系在了一起。

lines.en: M: Thank you. Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades. We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body. As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least 85% score in the entrance exam. Do you think you can attain this?
lines.zh: M：谢谢。现在我想谈谈你的学业经历和预期成绩。我们愿意把自己看作一所享有盛誉的院校，拥有一批竞争力强、前途光明的学生。你知道，要进入我们的课程，入学考试至少要考到85%。你觉得自己能达到这个分数吗？

lines.en: W: I think so. Yes.
lines.zh: W：我想可以。是的。

lines.en: M: I'm looking at your school grades now and I'll be honest. It's a bit of a mixed bag. You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned, our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.
lines.zh: M：我现在正在看你的在校成绩，我直说吧，情况有好有坏。你有些科目成绩确实很优秀，但你并不是很……怎么说呢，“稳定”？我不介意有条件地录取你，但你要做好心理准备，我们的入学考试，用你自己的话说，可不是件轻松的事。

lines.en: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon. If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised. More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
lines.zh: 登录电子邮箱账户有时感觉就像试图入侵五角大楼。如果遵循所有指南，你需要为每个账户使用不同的密码；使用由字母、数字和符号组成的令人难以理解的组合；注册两步验证；并且每当其中一个密码遭到泄露时，就更改所有密码。更常见的是，接下来你还必须选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向电脑提供确凿证据，证明你确实是人类。

lines.en: It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys. Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon. Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it. Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often. The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
lines.zh: 难怪我们大多数人忘记密码的次数比忘记钥匙的次数还多。如今，芬兰阿尔托大学的研究人员开展了一项新的同行评议研究，试图弄清我们为何会忘记密码，以帮助终结这一令人沮丧的现象。他们的研究结果表明，你记住密码的可能性有多大，与密码本身的关系较小，而更多地取决于你预期使用它的频率。也就是说，如果你知道自己会经常使用一个复杂密码登录某个账户，那么你记住它的可能性要远高于记住一个简单密码的可能性，后者所对应的账户是你预计不会经常登录的。研究人员建议网站为用户更频繁登录提供更多激励，以帮助他们记住自己的密码。

lines.en: Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump. She wanted to improve her physical and mental health. However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training programme to follow. When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging; she avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights. A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question. The extravagant cost was just unaffordable. She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics. To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals. A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime. After the workout, the app's artificial intelligence software system gives feedback from Ms. Weiner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions. Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting. This is because no two are ever the same. As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms. The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results. However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. An app cannot understand human behavior. It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness. Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout. He can also make exercise fun and sustainable. Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly. This can safeguard against injuries. An app cannot perceive such subtleties.
lines.zh: 四年前，Jenny Weiner 的身体状况正处于低谷。她希望改善自己的身心健康。然而，由于没有适当的训练计划可供遵循，她的锻炼缺乏强度。她去健身房时，每天的锻炼主要都选择慢跑之类的轻松项目；而像举重这样更具挑战性的运动，她则避而远之。请一位能够督促她的私人教练更是不可能的事，因为高昂的费用实在负担不起。后来，她发现了健身手机应用 Slimmeretics。要使用这款应用，首先需要输入个人资料，包括以往的训练经历和偏好，以及期望达到的目标。随后，虚拟教练会利用这些信息为用户制定个性化的训练方案。锻炼结束后，这款应用的人工智能软件系统会根据 Weiner 女士以及全球其他5300万名用户的反馈，调整未来的训练安排。如今，Weiner 女士觉得锻炼很令人兴奋。这是因为每次锻炼都不尽相同。因此，这款应用帮助她减重超过25公斤。该应用采用数学方法，可以安排更加细致周密的锻炼计划，从而取得最佳效果。然而，一些专家认为，应用程序无法取代人类私人教练。应用程序无法理解人类行为，也无法明白除了健康和健身之外，人们还会面临其他相互竞争的需求。此外，人类教练可以在锻炼中融入关怀，也能让运动变得有趣且可持续。教练可以监督一个人是否正确完成动作，从而防止受伤。应用程序无法察觉这些细微之处。

lines.en: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded. Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
lines.zh: 牛津大学得出结论，所有社会都由七条普遍的道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从上级和尊重他人财产。尽管许多文化正朝着更加自由、等级制度更弱的组织形式发展，但这项新研究表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善和兄弟情谊等基本价值观，才是成功社会的基石。

lines.en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
lines.zh: 这项针对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有群体都遵循七项基本的道德准则。这些普遍规则是：帮助家人，帮助群体，回报他人的帮助，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，以及尊重他人的财产。研究人员发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者群体，还是先进文明，各类社会都重视这些品格；这些品格有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。“每个地方的每个人都拥有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说，“这七条道德规则之所以在不同文化中都具有普遍性，是因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即便其中一些品格看起来属于右翼或保守立场，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会表现出对某个群体的忠诚，以及对某个人或某种事物的服从。这表明，真正将我们联结在一起的因素多于分裂我们的因素。”

lines.en: The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world. They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics. However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others. Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ. Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data. "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said. "These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing. In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field."
lines.zh: 这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究，是迄今开展的规模最大、最全面且覆盖范围最广的道德调查，旨在 выяс明不同社会是否拥有不同版本的道德观。研究团队查阅了世界上最权威的档案资料，分析了来自世界各地60个社会的600多份资料记载。他们发现，在所有社会中，这七条规则都被视为合乎道德的准则，并且在各大洲、各种宗教和不同政治体系中都得到遵守。不过，一些群体对某些规则的重视程度高于其他规则。柯里博士希望，这项研究能够促进不同文化之间的相互理解，帮助人们认识到彼此的共同点，以及我们存在差异的方式和原因。合著者哈维·怀特豪斯教授表示，社会科学家现在应当着手在实地检验这一理论，而不是依赖旧数据。他说：“这项研究建立在对世界各地文化的历史描述之上。这些描述是在独立于我们所检验的理论、且早于该理论提出的情况下形成的。今后，如果社会科学家认真对待道德理论的检验，就需要在实地以更加系统的方式收集新数据。”

lines.en: When it comes to food, color is money. Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings. Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards. And oranges are just the beginning. There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.
lines.zh: 说到食品，颜色就是金钱。食品公司深知，颜色越好，价格就越高，因此它们会确保产品的色泽具有吸引力，以增加收益。例如，橙子必须符合特定的色泽标准。而橙子还只是开始。包括炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃在内的食品，都有相应的色泽标准。

lines.en: The attention to color is for good reason. For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
lines.zh: 人们之所以如此重视颜色，是有充分理由的。尽管人们总是在谈论舌头，但我们的眼睛实际上可能是饮食体验中最重要的部分。我们大脑的大量功能都用于处理视觉信息，而分配给味觉功能的只有百分之一或百分之二，其结果是，颜色确实会改变我们品尝食物时的感受。

lines.en: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste. In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage. Only one in five was able to identify it as orange. But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor. And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange. None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color. What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color? Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues? Or does color actually change the experience of taste? The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation. The brain makes predictions using color. These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience. Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like. So we need to learn this over time. The brain gets information from the environment. And we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet. Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
lines.zh: 科学家多次证明了颜色对味觉的重要性。例如，在20世纪80年代的一项研究中，实验参与者被要求说出所饮用饮料的味道，但他们无法看到饮料本身。只有五分之一的人能够辨认出那是橙子味。然而，当他们可以看到自己所饮用的饮料，而饮料呈橙色时，每个人都辨认出了橙子味。当一杯青柠味饮料被染成橙色时，近一半的受访者将饮料的味道辨认为橙子味。而当饮料呈绿色时，没有人犯这样的错误。当一个人无法辨认出自己看不见的饮料，或颜色异常的饮料的味道时，究竟发生了什么？是因为参与者无法分辨出它是什么味道，所以依赖视觉线索吗？还是颜色确实改变了味觉体验？这些问题的关键在于颜色对预期的影响。大脑会利用颜色作出预测，而这些预测依赖于来自经验的预期。研究表明，我们生来就喜欢甜食，也渴望食用甜食，但我们并不是天生就知道自己渴望的甜食看起来是什么样子。因此，我们需要随着时间的推移逐渐学会这一点。大脑从环境中获取信息。例如，我们会了解到，水果会从绿色、酸涩变成红色、成熟和甜美。因此，如果我们看到一颗绿色的浆果，就会将其颜色与酸味联系起来；而仅仅看到一个红色的水果，就会激活我们对其味道甜美可口的预期。

lines.en: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives. For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal. And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
lines.zh: 寻找意义是我们许多人一生都会经历的事情。对一些人来说，这种意义是宗教上的；对一些人来说，是政治上的；对另一些人来说，则是人际关系方面的。而拥有意义感能够带给我们幸福。

lines.en: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources. Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries. The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015. Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot or experienced a lot of happiness. Meaning was measured through a daily "purpose index", which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals. Finally, income levels were assessed. The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets. But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker. The second study looked at worldwide data. Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: "Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?" Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets. In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person. Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a "social ladder", representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career. The results from the study duplicated those of the first two.
lines.zh: 一项新研究考察了在财务资源背景下意义与幸福之间的关系。多伦多大学的里娅·卡塔帕诺及其同事发现，对于富裕人群而言，意义是幸福感的预测因素，其作用远弱于对较贫困人群的作用，这表明经济资源可能会影响我们体验意义的方式。研究团队分析了来自123个国家的50多万人的数据。第一项研究使用了2013年至2015年间收集的美国居民每日民意调查数据。研究人员通过积极情绪指标追踪幸福感，即调查前一天，参与者是否曾多次微笑或大笑，或体验到很强的幸福感。意义感则通过每日的“目标指数”进行测量，该指数考察参与者在多大程度上觉得自己喜欢每天所做的事情，并且有动力实现自己的目标。最后，研究人员评估了收入水平。结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在收入较低的人群中最强。但随着收入水平提高，这种相关性逐渐减弱。第二项研究考察了全球数据。幸福感采用与第一项研究相同的问题进行测量，而意义感则通过一个单一问题进行测量：“你是否觉得自己的生活具有重要的目标或意义？”同样，意义与幸福之间关系的强弱取决于参与者的收入：与收入较高的人群相比，意义对低收入人群幸福感的影响更大。在最后一项研究中，法国参与者表明了自己在多大程度上觉得过着有目标且有意义的生活，以及他们在多大程度上认为自己是一个幸福的人。最后，他们没有按照具体收入阶层进行划分，而是将自己置于一架“社会阶梯”上，以代表自己在社会中就财富、教育和职业而言所处的位置。该研究的结果与前两项研究的结果一致。

lines.en: So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more. This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community. Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important.
lines.zh: 总的来说，资源较少的人群中，意义与幸福之间的关系比资源较多的人群更强。这可能是因为富裕人士更容易获得其他幸福来源，其中许多来源是外部的，例如较少的压力或社区支持。因此，对内在满足感、目标感或意义感的关注就没有那么重要了。

analysis.定位: P1 Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting. This is because no two are ever the same. 如今韦纳女士觉得训练很有意思。这是因为没有任何两次训练是相同的。
analysis.信号: 因果信号 This is because 紧跟其后的句子即原因。原文先说她觉得训练有趣，紧接 This is because no two are ever the same. 用因果信号 This is because 引出原因——没有两次训练是一样的，正是本题答案落点。
analysis.替换: no two are ever the same↔They are never repeated.肯否结构转换："没有两次相同" = "从不重复"，意思等值
analysis.排除: B)答非所问They help enrich her life. 听来正面、也像 app 的好处，但题问的是 "为何觉得训练 exciting"，原文给的原因明确是 no two are ever the same，而非 "丰富生活"；该项答的是别的问题。 C)原词陷阱They are of no extreme intensity. 借用了原文 her workouts lacked intensity 中的 intensity，可那句讲的是四年前训练缺乏强度的旧问题，与 "现在为何觉得有趣" 无关，听到 intensity 就选即中招。 借用原文：her workouts lacked intensity D)原词陷阱They keep her focused on her goal. 借用原文 your desired goals 里的 goal，可原文谈 goal 只是说输入资料时填写目标，并未把 "专注目标" 说成她觉得训练有趣的原因，原因仍是 no two are ever the same。 借用原文：your desired goals

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do some experts think of fitness apps like Slimmeretics?
questions.stem_zh: 一些专家如何看待像Slimmeretics这样的健身应用程序?

analysis.定位: P1 However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. 然而，一些专家认为这些 app 无法取代真人私人教练。
analysis.信号: 转折 However + 评价主体 some experts 直接表态。原文前面一直夸 app 效果好，However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. 用转折 However 转向、并由评价主体 some experts 直陈观点，转折后才是本题真意。
analysis.替换: apps cannot replace human personal trainers↔They will not be able to take the place of human personal trainers.近义短语替换：replace = take the place of，human personal trainers 原样保留
analysis.排除: B)原词陷阱They will not be able to comprehend some of the profiles users put in. 借用了原文 It will not comprehend that there are competing interests 的 comprehend，以及输入环节的 profile，可原文说 app 不能理解的是 "人类行为/相互竞争的利益"，而非看不懂用户填的 profiles，对象被偷换。 借用原文：It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness. C)与原文相反They cannot lead to optimal results with their mathematical approach. 盗用了原文 mathematical approach 与 optimal results，可原文是正面说 The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results.——数学方法"能"带来最优结果，选项加了 cannot 把极性反了。 借用原文：The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results. D)与原文相反They cannot match humans in arranging meticulous workout schedules. 借用原文 meticulous workout schedule，可原文是正面称 The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.——app 能编排更精细的计划，并非说它在这点上不如真人，方向相反。 借用原文：The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers?
questions.stem_zh: 我们从牛津大学研究人员的结论中了解到什么？

analysis.定位: P1 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded. 牛津大学得出结论：所有社会都靠七条普世道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从尊长、尊重他人财物。
analysis.信号: 结论标志词 concluded。句末的 Oxford University has concluded 是明确的结论信号，加之这句出现在篇章开头点题处，正是篇章独白把核心论点摆在开头的典型位置，听到 concluded 就该锁定这句是答案句。
analysis.替换: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules↔All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rulesheld together 同义改写为 kept together
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values. 把第一段后文的 basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies 的原词 cornerstones、basic values 搬了过来，但那句讲的是成功社会的基石，并非研究的总结论本身，听到熟词就选会落进这个陷阱。 借用原文：basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies B)偷换概念Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits. 借了原文出现过的 seven 和第二段的 The character traits held for every kind of community，但研究的结论说的是七条道德规则（rules），而非七种性格特质，把 rules 偷换成 character traits 就跑偏了。 借用原文：The character traits held for every kind of community D)偷换概念Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard. 用了第二段 Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code 的熟悉句式，但原文说的是共享一套七条规则的道德准则（code），D 把它笼统说成 a universal moral standard，丢掉了结论里七条规则这一核心，不如 C 精确对应题干问的结论。 借用原文：Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code

locate.en: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
locate.zh: 牛津大学得出结论：所有社会都靠七条普世道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从尊长、尊重他人财物。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do?
questions.stem_zh: 牛津研究人员的新研究旨在做什么？

analysis.定位: P3 The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. 这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面、覆盖最广的道德调查，旨在弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。
analysis.信号: 意图标志 aimed to find out。句中的 aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality 用 aimed to 直陈研究目的，这是目的题最直接的信号，听到 aimed to 即可锁定。
analysis.替换: aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality↔Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality近乎原句，仅去掉 aimed to
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people. 把第二段 Dr. Curry 那句里的 deferring to authority 和 right-wing 原词搬来，但那是他举例说明规则的普世性，并非这项研究本身要弄清的目标，听到熟词就选会被带偏。 借用原文：deferring to authority C)偷换概念Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues. 听上去和研究目的沾边，但原文目的是查不同社会是否有不同版本的道德，C 反向说成所有社会是否面对相同道德问题，方向被改了。 借用原文：whether different societies had different versions of morality D)原词陷阱Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty. 借了第二段 left-wing people will still have a group loyalty 的原话，但那是 Dr. Curry 论证规则普世性的例子，不是研究要查明的目标，属典型的盗用原句却答非所问。 借用原文：left-wing people will still have a group loyalty

locate.en: The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
locate.zh: 这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面、覆盖最广的道德调查，旨在弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to theories of morality?
questions.stem_zh: Harvey Whitehouse认为社会科学家应该如何对待道德理论？

analysis.定位: P3 In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field. 今后，社会科学家若真要检验道德理论，就需要更系统地到实地去采集新数据。
analysis.信号: 建议信号 will need to + 转折 rather than。Whitehouse 先说 should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data，再用 they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field 点明做法；need to 是建议信号，rather than relying on old data 则用对比把落点推向新数据。
analysis.替换: gather new data, more systematically, out in the field↔Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.systematically 名词化、out in the field 转为 field studies
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world. 搬了原文 These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing 的原词 independent、descriptions，但那是在说本研究所依据的旧资料的来历，不是 Whitehouse 主张今后该做的事，时间方向相反。 借用原文：These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing B)张冠李戴Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples. 借了第三段 Dr. Curry 那句 appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ 的差异话题，但那是 Curry 的期望，且题干问的是 Whitehouse 的主张，张冠李戴又跑了题。 借用原文：appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ C)与原文相反Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data. 里的 existing data 恰是 Whitehouse 用 rather than relying on old data 明确否定的对象，他主张采集新数据，C 取了被否定的旧数据一侧，方向反了。 借用原文：rather than relying on old data

locate.en: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field.
locate.zh: 今后，社会科学家若真要检验道德理论，就需要更系统地到实地去采集新数据。

option_analysis.reason: Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world. 搬了原文 These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing 的原词 independent、descriptions，但那是在说本研究所依据的旧资料的来历，不是 Whitehouse 主张今后该做的事，时间方向相反。
Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples. 借了第三段 Dr. Curry 那句 appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ 的差异话题，但那是 Curry 的期望，且题干问的是 Whitehouse 的主张，张冠李戴又跑了题。
Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data. 里的 existing data 恰是 Whitehouse 用 rather than relying on old data 明确否定的对象，他主张采集新数据，C 取了被否定的旧数据一侧，方向反了。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the speaker say about our eyes?
questions.stem_zh: 讲话者关于我们的眼睛说了什么?

analysis.定位: P2 For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. 尽管人们老在谈论舌头（的味觉），我们的眼睛或许才真正是吃这件事里最重要的部分。
analysis.信号: 让步 For all… + 强调 really might。信号是句首让步结构 For all the talk of the tongue（"尽管都在说舌头"）后面才抛出真正主张，再加 our eyes really might be the most important part 里的 "really" 加重语气——让步之后、被强调的那句才是说话人的落点，正是答案句。
analysis.替换: our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience↔They might be the most important part of our eating experience.近乎原句、They 替 our eyes
analysis.排除: B)偷换概念B 盗用了第 2 段原词 brain functions。原文说 A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision——是 "很多脑功能用于处理视觉"，主语是脑功能、用来佐证 eyes 重要；B 把它倒过来说成 "眼睛激活脑功能"，还加了原文没有的 "in a most direct fashion"，是偷换概念，且没回答 "说话人对 eyes 的核心论断"。 借用原文：A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision C)未提及C 借用了关于眼睛的常见俗语 "心灵的窗户"，听着像常识、最易顺口选中，但整篇录音只把眼睛和 "eating experience（吃的体验）" 挂钩，从未说眼睛是 "心灵的窗户"，属原文未提及，凭常识选它就中招。 D)与原文相反D 说眼睛会 mislead us（误导我们），是贬义。但答案句对眼睛是高度肯定——our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience，说话人在抬高眼睛而非贬低。D 的态度与原文相反，故排除。 借用原文：our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience

cloze.title: 2024年12月·第1套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: With the rapid progress in the economy, it is natural that people's ideology is bound for change. Being __(26)__ is no longer a virtue to some people, and they are not alone in holding this view. Each might have different viewpoints on how to lead one's lifestyle: some prefer simplicity, some love luxuries, some spend __(27)__ , some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse. As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its __(28)__ to me, but as my station changes, I have an opportunity to __(29)__ with the newly rich, an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle.
passages.zh: 随着经济的迅速发展，人们的思想观念必然会发生变化。对一些人来说，节俭不再是一种美德，而且持有这种看法的并非只有他们。每个人对于如何安排自己的生活方式可能都有不同的观点：有些人喜欢简朴，有些人钟爱奢侈，有些人挥霍无度，有些人则像乡下老鼠一样尽可能多地积攒财富。我出身贫寒，生于农村，淳朴的乡村生活很少会失去对我的吸引力；但随着我的社会地位发生变化，我有机会与新贵们交往，这段经历彻底改变了我对生活方式的看法。

passages.en: It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much, an idea only recently being revealed to me. Actually the whole world is in a __(30)__ to borrow and to spend, with the USA leading the trend. The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world, but the __(31)__ is that they borrow money from us. Though a __(32)__ of economics, at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into the __(33)__ rather than the decent and kind lender. An apparent case is real estate. Those who are __(34)__ and have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. Even education is not immune from this theory. Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this investment, even though they have to __(35)__ a living. It is reasonable to conclude that spending is praiseworthy, supposing it is not beyond your means.
passages.zh: 少花钱、多储蓄是邪恶的，甚至是有罪的，这是我最近才认识到的一种观念。实际上，全世界都在疯狂地借贷和消费，而美国引领了这一潮流。美国仍然是世界上最富有、最强大的国家，但具有讽刺意味的是，他们却向我们借钱。虽然我不是经济学专业人士，但至少我知道，用借来的钱进行投资，会使借款人成为掠夺者，而不是体面善良的贷款人。房地产就是一个明显的例子。那些精明且从银行获得贷款的人，会把买来的房屋以高出数倍的价格卖掉，从而变得相对富有。甚至教育也无法摆脱这一理论的影响。许多贫困的父母虽然只能勉强维持生计，但他们有远见，将子女送进大学，并从这项投资中获益。假定消费没有超出你的经济能力，可以合理地得出结论：消费是值得称赞的。

wordbank.gloss: n. 吸引力；呼吁；v. 有吸引力，呼吁
n. 讽刺，反讽；具有讽刺意味的事
adj. 恶意的，怀有恶意的
v. 混合，交往，相互结识
n. 捕食者；掠夺者，剥削者
n. 盛怒；时尚，风靡一时的事物（in a rage to do = 急切地、狂热地）；v. 发怒

rows.text: O) thrifty形容词
Being ___ 是动名词作主语，空位须填形容词作表语
全文主题是「省与花」，被评为美德的正是「节俭」 结合 overview 与下一段 It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much，作者反思的正是把「节俭/少花多存」当美德这件事；此处需要一个表「节俭」的形容词，thrifty 精准对应；它也与第 27 题的 extravagantly 形成全文核心对照。

G)majestic「雄伟的」与个人生活态度无关 majestic 多用于山河、宫殿等宏伟事物，描述人时也偏「庄严威严」，与「美德/生活习惯」的语义场不沾边。 H)malicious感情色彩反了——它是贬义 malicious 意为「心怀恶意的」，是贬义词；而后文紧跟 a virtue（美德），褒贬色彩冲突，直接排除。 N)shrewd「精明」更偏处世手腕，且第 34 题更需要它 shrewd 指头脑精明、会算计，并不直接对应「省钱」这一道德范畴；而且本卷第 34 题 Those who are __(34)__ and have got loans from the bank 在「精明地借贷投资房产」的语境里几乎只能由 shrewd 填上，先做易空的策略告诉我们 shrewd 要留给第 34 题。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— shrewd 也是形容词，且常被夸为美德。shrewd 既是形容词、又含「精明」这一常被视作褒义的特质，很容易被误填到 Being __(26)__ is no longer a virtue to some people；防坑点：本卷主旨是「省 vs 花」，第 34 题更需要 shrewd，先看全文再回填，节俭（thrifty）才是和「a virtue」「spend little and save much」前后呼应的那个。
B) extravagantly副词
动词 spend 后缺修饰语，要填副词

与前文 luxuries、后文 accumulate 形成对照 前一分句 some love luxuries 已立「奢华爱好」，下一分句 some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse 立「拼命攒钱」；本空在「花钱方式」的维度上需要一个「挥霍地、毫无节制地」的副词，与「攒钱」形成强对比，extravagantly（奢侈地、挥霍地）正好对应。

C)intrinsically「本质上」与「花钱方式」无关 intrinsically 描述「事物的内在属性」，搭配 spend 既不构成常见用法，也讲不通「本质地花钱」这种意思，与前后并列项的「花钱风格」维度对不上。 F)literally「字面意义上」无法与 spend 直接搭出对照 literally 用于强调「真的、确确实实」，常修饰带夸张色彩的动词短语，但此处需要的是「花钱的程度/方式」对照「攒钱」，literally spend 无法形成对比意义，方向偏离。
A) appeal名词
形容词性物主代词 its 后接名词
lose one's appeal to sb.＝对某人失去吸引力 lose one's appeal to sb. 是固定搭配；结合 As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its __(28)__ to me——「简单的乡村生活对我从未失去吸引力」，语义自洽，搭配地道。

D)irony「讽刺」与「失去」搭配方向不对 lose its irony 表「失去讽刺意味」，与「乡村生活对我」之间没有「讽刺」可言，且第 31 题 the irony is that... 是高度匹配 irony 的句型，应留给第 31 题。 E)layman「外行」是指人，不能作生活的属性 layman 指「门外汉」，是描述人的身份名词，不会被「乡村生活」拥有；且第 32 题 a ___ of economics 是典型 a layman of 用法，应留给那里。 I)meadow「草地」是具体物，不能被「失去」 meadow 是具体名词（草地、牧场），代入 lose its meadow 完全讲不通——乡村生活不会「失去它的一块草地」。 K)predator「掠夺者」与本句感情色彩冲突 predator 多含贬义「掠食者/剥削者」，与「乡村生活对我从未失去 ___」这种偏温情的语境冲突；且第 33 题 turn the borrower into the ___ rather than the decent and kind lender 明显需要它形成对照，应留给第 33 题。 L)rage「盛怒/风潮」与「乡村生活对我」不搭 rage 作名词表「盛怒」或「时尚风潮」，lose its rage 不构成英文常见搭配，且语义与「乡村生活的吸引力」无关；第 30 题 in a rage to do 的固定结构更需要它。
J) mingle动词
have an opportunity to ___ 中 to 后接动词原形
mingle with sb. 是「与人交往」的固定搭配 mingle with the newly rich 即「与新富阶层打交道」，正是作者所说的 an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle.——能改变其生活观的，只有「亲身接触」这件事，语义、搭配双双契合。

M)scrapescrape 不与 with sb. 搭配「交往」 scrape 作动词意为「刮、擦、勉强凑集」，常见搭配是 scrape by/along/a living，并不存在 scrape with sb. 表示与人交往的用法；而且第 35 题 they have to __(35)__ a living 恰好是 scrape a living 的经典搭配，先做易空策略提示要把 M 留给第 35 题。
L) rage名词
be in a ___ to do sth. 中 a 后接名词
in a rage to do＝狂热地、风靡地做某事 rage 作名词除「盛怒」外，常指「时尚、风靡一时的事物」；in a rage to borrow and to spend 即「世界都疯狂地借钱、花钱」，与后文 with the USA leading the trend（trend 也是同义复现）完全呼应。
I)meadow「草地」与「全世界都在借钱花钱」毫无关联 meadow 是具体名词且语义场完全脱节，代入后 in a meadow to borrow 不成句，立即排除。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— meadow 看似与 borrow/spend 无关却最容易被排除得太晚。in a meadow 听上去像「在一片草地上」，部分考生扫到 the whole world is in a ___ 时可能短暂迷惑；防坑点：be in a ___ to do sth. 是固定结构，后接表「热潮/狂热」的抽象名词，meadow 不在此类，看 to do 这条线就能立排。
D) irony名词
定冠词 the 后＋is 前，须是名词作主语
「最强最富却向别人借钱」恰是反讽 前一句 The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world，紧接 but the irony is that they borrow money from us——「最富最强反而要向我们借钱」正是「反讽」最典型的用法；the irony is that... 也是英语固定句型。

E)layman「外行」无法承担 the ___ is that... 的语义 the layman is that... 不成立，layman 是指人，无法被引出「事实」的句型使用。 I)meadow「草地」与 borrow money 无关 meadow 是具体名词，与「美国借钱」的话题完全脱节，语义不接。 K)predator「掠夺者」做主语后接 is that 不通 predator 也是指人/动物的名词，the predator is that they borrow money from us 在意思上不通，且第 33 题 turn the borrower into the ___ 才是它的归宿。 L)rage「盛怒/风潮」不能承担 the ___ is that... 的「事实/反差」语义 the rage is that... 不构成英文中表达「事实/反讽」的句型；且第 30 题 in a rage to do 的固定结构更需要它。
E) layman名词
Though a ___ of economics 是名词性短语作让步状语
a layman of economics＝经济学外行 作者紧接说 at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into...——「虽是外行，但至少懂得……」，前后形成「让步＋让步内的肯定」逻辑；layman of 是「某领域的外行」的常见说法。

I)meadow「草地」不能修饰人的身份 meadow 不指人，与 Though I am a meadow of economics 完全不通，词义层面就排除。 K)predator「掠夺者」与作者自谦语气冲突 predator 多用于贬义的「掠食者/掠夺者」，且后文紧跟 at least I know that... 这种「自谦但仍有见识」的口吻，搭配 predator 在语气和语义上都冲突；且第 33 题更需要它。 L)rage「盛怒/风潮」不能描述人在某学科的身份 rage 作名词不指人，a rage of economics 不构成「某学科的人」这种用法；第 30 题 in a rage to do 才是它的归宿。
K) predator名词
turn A into the ___ rather than the decent and kind lender 中 the 后名词
predator vs. lender＝掠夺者 vs. 仁慈的放贷人 the decent and kind lender 是「正派善良的放贷人」，与之对照、且语义反向的恰是 predator（掠夺者/剥削者）；句意：「借钱投资会把借款人变成掠夺者，而非正派的放贷人」，与作者「借钱投资可致富」的论点完全一致。

I)meadow「草地」无法与「放贷人」并列对照 meadow 是具体名词，rather than 两端必须同类，meadow 与 lender 不同类，直接排除。 L)rage「盛怒」也不指人，无法与 lender 同类并列 rage 作名词指「盛怒」或「风潮」，不指人，与 lender 不同类，无法承担 rather than 两端的对照；且第 30 题 in a rage to do 才是它的归宿。
N) shrewd形容词
Those who are ___ and have got loans 中 are 后＋and 并列谓语，空位须为形容词
「精明」恰好描述会借贷投资房产致富的人 shrewd 意为「精明的、有眼光的」，与下文 have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. 描述的「从银行贷款 → 倒卖房产 → 致富」的精明操作完全契合。
G)majestic「雄伟」不能形容人的投资能力 majestic 多用于山川、宫殿等宏伟事物，做表语形容人时偏「庄严威严」，与「会贷款投资房产」的精明操作无关。 H)malicious贬义「恶意」与「合法投资致富」语境冲突 malicious 是「怀有恶意的」，但本句并未对借贷投资者作道德谴责，只是陈述「精明者→致富」的因果，贬义色彩不合适。
M) scrape动词
they have to ___ a living 中 to 后接动词原形带宾语

scrape a living＝勉强糊口的固定搭配 上下文 Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this investment, even though they have to __(35)__ a living. 说穷父母为送孩子上大学不惜「勉强糊口」，scrape a living 是六级常考的固定搭配，含义完全契合「贫困到只够维持生活」的语境。

longreading.title: 2024年12月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles(腌菜) and salads. "It's not very well-known," says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan(龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. "We have to grow what is profitable," he says.
passages.zh: 在马六甲海峡附近的一座小型水果农场里，Lim Kok Ann 只剩下一棵还在生长的酸果树。这种果实口感脆爽、味道酸涩，马来西亚人主要用它制作腌菜和沙拉。这位45岁的农民说：“它不太为人所知。”相反，他正专注于种植市场更大的龙眼和菠萝。“我们必须种植有利可图的作物。”他说。

passages.en: B) But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. They're pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called "alternative" crops—such as kedondong. At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. "Anything you see here is a forgotten crop," says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur.
passages.zh: 然而，距离这里不到一小时车程的马来西亚乡间，在三座巨大的银色穹顶内，科学家们正努力改变食物的未来。他们通过种植和加工所谓的“替代性”作物，例如酸果，来拓展人类食物的边界。在全球研究中心“未来作物”（Crops For the Future，CFF）的总部，这种一度未被充分利用的水果已经被制成无糖果汁，富含维生素C，并在感官评价中获得了最高评价。“你在这里看到的任何东西，都是一种被遗忘的作物。”在马来西亚首都吉隆坡郊外、CFF花园里生长的各种繁茂植物间，Sayed Azam-Ali 说道。

passages.en: C) Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. "We're dependent on these four," he says. "But actually there're 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops—plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or "alternative" as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.
passages.zh: Azam-Ali 教授解释说，仅小麦、玉米、水稻和大豆这四种作物，就提供了世界粮食供应量的三分之二。“我们依赖这四种作物。”他说，“但实际上，我们已经耕种了7,000种作物数千年。我们却忽视了它们。”研究人员正努力挖掘这些被忽视作物的潜力。这些植物被他们称为被遗忘的、未充分利用的或“替代性”作物，因为随着以主要作物加工原料为基础的饮食日益趋同，它们逐渐被排挤。

passages.en: D) It's a timely quest. The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.
passages.zh: 这项探索来得正是时候。目前，粮食部门造成的温室气体排放量已经接近全球总排放量的三分之一。据估计，到2050年，为了养活预计达到100亿的全球人口，世界必须多生产50%的食物。在不助长气候变化的情况下满足这一需求，需要紧迫的解决方案。

passages.en: E) Forgotten crops hold key answers. By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient(具有气候韧性的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. His summary is plain: "Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity."
passages.zh: 被遗忘的作物蕴含着解决问题的关键答案。通过投资于被忽视的本地植物，各国可以减少对进口作物及其高碳供应链的依赖。让人类曾经食用的作物多样性重新回归，也能在变暖的气候威胁现有作物之际提升粮食安全。除此之外，Azam-Ali 认为，被遗忘的作物是最具气候韧性、营养最丰富的作物之一。他的总结十分明确：“饮食多样化对人类的未来至关重要。”

passages.en: F) Food security experts agree. "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds.
passages.zh: 粮食安全专家对此表示认同。“世界上不存在粮食不安全，存在的是对食物的无知。”新加坡国立大学水政策研究所高级研究员 Cecilia Tortajada 说道。“每当我们拥有本土作物时，往往会忽视它们，仿佛它们毫无价值，但事实上它们是有价值的。”她补充道。

passages.en: G) Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. But "the resistance was enormous," he recalls.
passages.zh: Azam-Ali 对这种怀疑深有体会。20世纪80年代，他通过自己在尼日尔结识的女性农民的工作，接触到了替代性作物。这位当时的博士生记得，自己对她们在自家庭院里种植的作物感到惊叹：即使没有技术支持，在主要作物歉收时，她们仍能依靠这些作物养活家人。他看到了建立替代性食物体系的巨大机会。但他回忆说：“阻力非常大。”

passages.en: H) Undeterred, he ploughed on. Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. "That's the critical thing," he says. In one of the centre's domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa(辣木) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten(谷胶) and higher in nutrients. Tan's job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. "I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes." says Tan, who is also a trained chef. It's a strategy to appeal to the world's growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. It's also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as "old or poor people's food" or as inferior "women's crops", adds Tan.
passages.zh: 他没有因此却步，而是继续推进。一项又一项的项目帮助证明，这些作物在不同环境中可以作为主食作物的替代品种植。然而，这些作物能否适应市场的问题仍然存在。“这才是关键。”他说。在该中心的一座穹顶内，食品技术专家 Tan Xinlin 用辣木叶粉替代部分小麦粉，烘焙出一种麸质含量更低、营养成分更高的蛋糕。Tan 的工作是利用这些仍不为人熟悉的原料制作食谱，使其同时迎合本地和国际口味。近年来，她一直使用CFF种植的一些被遗忘的作物，例如辣木和班巴拉花生，制作从速食汤到印度小吃的各种食品。“我努力让被遗忘的作物现代化，而不是使用旧食谱。”同样受过厨师训练的 Tan 说道。这种策略旨在吸引世界上不断壮大的中产阶级，他们越来越多地转向快餐和加工食品行业。Tan 补充说，这也是一种帮助消除人们对本地作物的看法的方式，即认为它们是“老年人或穷人的食物”，或是不如其他作物的“女性作物”。

passages.en: I) The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.
passages.zh: 人们对本地食物的这些负面联想，其根源可能十分深远。班巴拉花生是一种富含蛋白质的撒哈拉以南非洲本土作物，在东南亚部分地区也有种植，它的边缘化可以追溯到殖民统治时期。“种植班巴拉花生的非洲女性实际上会因种植它而受到惩罚。”Azam-Ali 说道。“殖民势力说，你们不能种这种作物，因为它不产油。我们无法为它找到市场。”然而如今，班巴拉花生制成的 murukku 是CFF评价最好的食品之一，研究人员正努力将其推向杂货店，并以藜麦等作物的成功为潜在投资者提供参考。大约30年前，在玻利维亚和秘鲁的原生山区之外，藜麦几乎无人知晓。如今，这种营养丰富的谷物已经出现在世界各地高级餐厅的菜单上。

passages.en: J) Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. Today "nutrition is becoming a time bomb", says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.
passages.zh: 以营养而非产量衡量作物，是被遗忘食物事业的核心。自20世纪60年代的“绿色革命”以来，高产作物一直主导着现代农业。这在一定程度上是对严重饥荒的重要回应，因为当时世界需要增加粮食供应。如今，随着不断升高的二氧化碳水平使作物流失矿物质，“营养正变成一枚定时炸弹。”Azam-Ali 说道。他坚称，与其对主要作物进行生物强化，我们不如投资于那些本身营养价值更高的被遗忘作物。

passages.en: K) In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre's "crown jewels", revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. This research is "the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that "future crops" are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.
passages.zh: 在CFF第三座穹顶的内部，实验室主管 Gomathy Sethuraman 打开一扇窗，展示该中心的“镇馆之宝”：在明亮的黄色灯光下生长的翼豆藤。这是多个实验室中的一个，科学家们在那里研究更高温度和更高二氧化碳水平对替代性作物营养成分的影响。Azam-Ali 说，这项研究是“改变游戏规则的因素”，能够确保“未来的作物”在更温暖的气候中也依然是最健康的作物。

passages.en: L) There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.
passages.zh: Food Tank 是一家总部位于美国的智库，其主席 Danielle Nierenberg 表示，全球对被遗忘食物的关注正日益形成势头。除了自称世界上第一个专门研究未充分利用作物的研究中心CFF之外，还有其他重要团体在倡导农业多样性，包括 Crop Trust、Slow Food、Icrisat 和 Bioversity International。她说，越来越多的中等收入消费者正在寻找营养丰富的食物，也有一些人渴望尝试祖父母辈曾经食用过的未经加工的食物，这些因素进一步推动了这一趋势。

passages.en: M) But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.
passages.zh: 然而，在一些地区，对被遗忘食物日益增长的兴趣，正被另一些地区全球扩散的西式饮食所压过；这种饮食含有大量糖、脂肪和加工食品。

passages.en: N) A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is "the obsession with imported products", says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a "status symbol", she says.
passages.zh: 例如，在马来西亚，推广逐渐消失的本地作物面临的一大障碍是“对进口产品的痴迷”。Jenifer Kuah 是一家倡导使用本地食材的餐厅的联合创始人，该餐厅位于吉隆坡一个富裕的郊区。她说，Sitka 被视为该国小型农场到餐桌餐饮领域的先驱，但那里的顾客仍然把外国食材当作“身份地位的象征”而加以追求。

passages.en: O) The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. "Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change," says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City, University of London. We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says.
passages.zh: 支持被遗忘食物的论据直观易懂。一些分析人士认为，这实际上是不可避免的。“气候变化几乎肯定会迫使人们改变口味。”伦敦大学城市学院食品政策教授 Tim Lang 说道。他说，随着主食作物的产量下降，我们“必须习惯食用其他作物”。

statements.en: According to a senior researcher, we will have secure food supply if we rid ourselves of ignorance about native crops.
statements.zh: 据一位资深研究员称,如果我们消除对本土作物的无知,我们将拥有安全的粮食供应。

analysis.定位: F 段 "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds. 「世界上不存在食物不安全，只存在食物无知，」 新加坡国立大学水政策研究所的资深研究员 Cecilia Tortajada 说。 「只要有本土作物，我们就倾向于无视它们，仿佛它们没有价值，但它们其实有价值，」 她补充说。
analysis.改写: a senior researcher↔a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore 身份同位替换 we will have secure food supply if we rid ourselves of ignorance about native crops↔There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance 否定对比 → 肯定因果重述 native crops↔native crops 原词复现

statements.en: Most of the world's food supply comes from a tiny number out of thousands of crops that have been grown for centuries.
statements.zh: 世界上大部分粮食供应来自数千种已种植了几个世纪的作物中的极少数作物。

analysis.锚点: 「a tiny number out of thousands」 的数量对比
analysis.定位: C 段 Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. "We're dependent on these four," he says. "But actually there're 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." Azam-Ali 教授解释说，仅仅小麦、玉米、稻米和大豆这四种作物就提供了全世界三分之二的食物供应。 「我们依赖这四种作物，」 他说， 「但其实我们已经种植了几千年的作物有 7000 种，我们对其他全都视而不见。」
analysis.改写: Most of the world's food supply↔two-thirds of the world's food supply 分数 → 模糊量词 a tiny number out of thousands of crops↔just four crops 具体小数 → 模糊小量词 that have been grown for centuries↔we've been farming for thousands of years 时间跨度的上下位
analysis.辨邻: D By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion 讲的是 「未来要多生产多少」，而非 「现在四种作物占多少」。 By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food

statements.en: To provide their family with food when the staple crops failed, some African women farmers grew local crops in their backyards.
statements.zh: 当主要作物歉收时,一些非洲女性农民在自家后院种植当地作物以为家人提供食物。

analysis.锚点: African women + backyards + 主粮失败
analysis.定位: G 段 He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. 他在 1980 年代通过在尼日尔遇到的妇女农人的工作接触到了替代作物。这位当时还在读博的学生回忆，对她们在自家后院、不借助科技、在主要作物失败时种来养家的作物，他充满惊叹。
analysis.改写: African women farmers↔women farmers he met in Niger 上位地理替换 grew local crops in their backyards↔the crops they grew in their backyards 原词复现 To provide their family with food when the staple crops failed↔to feed their families when the big crops failed 同义动词与上下位词替换
analysis.辨邻: I African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it 涉及的是 「殖民惩罚导致边缘化」 ，与 when the staple crops failed 这一动机条件无关。 African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it

statements.en: High-yielding crops have occupied a dominant position in modern agriculture since the green revolution in the last century.
statements.zh: 自上世纪绿色革命以来,高产作物在现代农业中占据主导地位。

analysis.定位: J 段 Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. 自 1960 年代的 「绿色革命」 以来，高产作物一直主导着现代农业。
analysis.改写: High-yielding crops↔high-yielding crops 原词复现 have occupied a dominant position in modern agriculture↔have dominated modern agriculture 动词与同源名词短语的等值替换 since the green revolution in the last century↔Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s 具体年代 → 上位时间段

statements.en: Growing alternative crops proved feasible in a variety of environments, but the critical question was whether they would be marketable.
statements.zh: 种植替代作物被证明在各种环境中是可行的,但关键问题是它们是否有市场。

analysis.定位: H 段 Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. 一个又一个项目帮助证明这些作物在不同环境中作为主粮的替代品是可行的。但它们是否能被市场接受这个问题仍然存在。
analysis.改写: Growing alternative crops proved feasible in a variety of environments↔Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones 形容词同义 + 名词同义 but the critical question was whether they would be marketable↔But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained 转折结构 + 关键词复现
analysis.辨邻: E By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops 是 「投资带来的好处」 的论述，没有 marketable 这一关键评估维度。 By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains

statements.en: According to a professor, when the yields of staple crops fall, we will have to adapt to eating foods from alternative crops.
statements.zh: 据一位教授称,当主要作物的产量下降时,我们将不得不适应食用来自替代作物的食物。

analysis.锚点: professor + 主粮减产 + 改吃替代作物
analysis.定位: O 段 We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says. 他说，随着主粮作物的产量下降，我们 「必须习惯吃别的作物」 。
analysis.改写: According to a professor↔Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City, University of London 身份具体化 when the yields of staple crops fall↔as yields of staple crops fall 连词同义替换 we will have to adapt to eating foods from alternative crops↔have to get used to eating other crops 动词短语同义 + 名词同义
analysis.辨邻: E warming climates threaten existing crops 后跟的是 「Bringing back the variety」 的主动倡议，而非 will have to adapt to eating 这种 「不得不适应」 的被动结论。 Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops

statements.en: Urgent measures have to be taken to provide food for the projected world population without aggravating the climate.
statements.zh: 必须采取紧急措施为预计的世界人口提供粮食,同时不加剧气候问题。

analysis.锚点: projected world population + 不加剧气候
analysis.定位: D 段 By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions. 据估计，到 2050 年，全世界必须多生产 50% 的食物，才能养活预计达到 100 亿的全球人口。在不加剧气候变化的前提下满足这一需求，需要紧急的解决方案。
analysis.改写: Urgent measures have to be taken↔calls for urgent solutions 「呼吁紧急方案」 与 「必须采取紧急措施」 等值 provide food for the projected world population↔to feed the projected global population of 10 billion 动词同义 + 形容词原词复现 without aggravating the climate↔without contributing to climate change 动词短语近义改写
analysis.辨邻: E Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity 是宣言式总结，缺 projected world population 与 Urgent measures 这两个具体要素。 Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity

statements.en: Colonial rule marginalised local crops by punishing Africans who grew them.
statements.zh: 殖民统治通过惩罚种植本土作物的非洲人使这些作物边缘化。

analysis.锚点: Colonial rule + punishing Africans + 种植
analysis.定位: I 段 "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." 「种植 bambara 花生的非洲妇女实际上因为种植它而受到惩罚，」 Azam-Ali 说。 「殖民列强说，你们不能种它，因为它不产油，我们没法给它打开市场。」
analysis.改写: Colonial rule↔Colonial powers 近义名词替换 marginalised local crops↔can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule 动词与同根名词的等值 by punishing Africans who grew them↔African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it 主动 → 被动 + 上下位人群
analysis.辨邻: G the crops they grew in their backyards … to feed their families when the big crops failed 描述的是 「主动求生式种植」 ，与 punishing Africans who grew them 这一 「被惩罚」 的因果链相反。 the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed

statements.en: As existing crops are endangered by global warming, we can increase food security by bringing back the many forgotten food crops.
statements.zh: 随着现有作物受到全球变暖的威胁,我们可以通过恢复许多被遗忘的粮食作物来增加粮食安全。

analysis.锚点: 全球变暖威胁现有作物 + 恢复被遗忘作物
analysis.定位: E 段 Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. 在气候变暖威胁现有作物之际，恢复人类曾经食用的多样化作物，也能提升食物安全。
analysis.改写: As existing crops are endangered by global warming↔at a time warming climates threaten existing crops 条件连词与谓语同义替换 we can increase food security↔boosts food security 动词同义替换 by bringing back the many forgotten food crops↔Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate 近义名词替换
analysis.辨邻: D Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions 提出问题，但没有 bringing back 这一具体对策。 Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions O have to get used to eating other crops 与 we can increase food security by bringing back the many forgotten food crops 在方向（被动适应 vs 主动恢复）与结论（习惯口味 vs 食物安全）上都不同。 have to get used to eating other crops

statements.en: Researchers are trying to find out how higher temperatures and CO₂ levels affect the nutritional composition of alternative crops.
statements.zh: 研究人员正在试图找出更高的温度和二氧化碳水平如何影响替代作物的营养成分。

analysis.定位: K 段 It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. 这是多个生长室之一，科学家们在那里研究更高温度与二氧化碳浓度对替代作物营养构成的影响。
analysis.改写: higher temperatures and CO₂ levels↔higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels 化学式与全称等值 the nutritional composition of alternative crops↔the nutritional make-up of alternative crops 近义名词替换 find out how … affect …↔studying the impact of … on … 句式重构
analysis.辨邻: J growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals 是结论式判断，与 Researchers are trying to find out 这一研究行为不同。 growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals

reading1.title: 2024年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
passages.zh: 想象一下，你是一名被派往地球、负责记录这个星球上哺乳动物行为的外星人。你偶然走进一家正在放映最新好莱坞恐怖电影的电影院。

passages.en: Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
passages.zh: 几十个人类聚集在一间昏暗而没有任何装饰的房间里。他们全都盯着一块矩形区域，那里光线的图案正在快速变化。

passages.en: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
passages.zh: 他们显然处于高度兴奋的状态。他们的心率加快，偶尔紧张地环顾四周，有时还会集体在座位上跳起来，并发出尖锐的警告声。

passages.en: Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
passages.zh: 最后，灯亮了，矩形屏幕变成了黑色。人类站起来离开房间，一边聊天大笑，一边流露出愉悦的迹象。

passages.en: Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
passages.zh: 为什么这些人类会自愿让自己经历这种看起来极其令人不快的体验？他们为什么会对屏幕上那些光线图案产生如此强烈的反应？

passages.en: I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
passages.zh: 我对恐怖的悖论着迷——许多人会主动寻求恐怖娱乐，这一事实十分奇怪。

passages.en: I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
passages.zh: 我认为，这个谜题的答案在于人性。

passages.en: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children's games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
passages.zh: 我的研究表明，我们人类经过进化，能够在安全的情境中体验负面情绪，并从中获得愉悦。你可以在儿童游戏中看到恐怖的这些要素。以捉迷藏为例，它是对捕食者与猎物互动的一种模拟。孩子躲起来，成年人假装成捕食者，一边像危险的野兽那样嚎叫，一边寻找孩子。

passages.en: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
passages.zh: 这种模拟为孩子提供了关于如何避免成为猎物的关键信息，而孩子往往会觉得这类活动非常令人满足，大概是因为它让孩子在安全的情况下体验了一个可能造成灾难的场景。

passages.en: They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
passages.zh: 他们会从中感到愉悦，而愉悦正是进化促使我们采取适应性行为的方式。

passages.en: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
passages.zh: 恐怖之所以能给许多人带来愉悦，是因为它让我们得以玩味负面情绪，并培养应对策略。我们会了解真正感到害怕是什么感觉，也会学会如何处理负面情绪。

passages.en: How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
passages.zh: 那么，恐怖是如何起作用的呢？我的研究表明，恐怖是通过利用一套古老的生物防御机制发挥作用的——这是一种经过进化形成的恐惧系统，我们与其他动物共同拥有这种系统。但人类具有独特的想象力，我们利用经过进化形成的想象力，进入充满危险的虚拟世界。

passages.en: There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?
passages.zh: 即使你不是忠实的恐怖片爱好者，观看恐怖电影也有充分的理由。如果你能完好无损地看完整部电影，你可能会产生强烈的掌控感，觉得自己成功熬过了一段骇人的经历。无论如何，观看恐怖电影会让你更善于应对自己的恐惧，而谁知道这种能力什么时候会变得至关重要呢？

questions.stem: The alien finds the audience in the movie theatre clearly in a state of ______.
questions.stem_zh: 外星人发现电影院里的观众明显处于______状态。

options.text: total mindfulness
options.zh: 完全专注

options.text: extreme excitement
options.zh: 极度兴奋

options.text: spiritual elevation
options.zh: 精神升华

options.text: intense curiosity
options.zh: 强烈好奇

questions.判型: The alien finds the audience in the movie theatre clearly in a state of ______ 问的是外星人眼中观众的客观状态，无 infer/imply/mainly 等抽象信号，是单点事实细节。
questions.拆句: Q46 句子主干是 The alien finds the audience ... in a state of ______，find sb. in a state of ... 是「发现某人处于某种状态」的复合宾语结构；clearly 修饰整个判断，强调状态显而易见；in the movie theatre 是 audience 的后置定语，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls. 他们显然处于一种高度唤起的状态。心率加快，偶尔紧张地四下张望，时不时在座位上一齐惊跳，并发出尖叫般的警示声。

locate.en: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
locate.zh: 他们显然处于一种高度唤起的状态。心率加快，偶尔紧张地四下张望，时不时在座位上一齐惊跳，并发出尖叫般的警示声。

option_analysis.note: total mindfulness 指「完全的正念/平静专注」，与 high arousal 描绘的生理躁动完全相反。
预判语义「高度兴奋」与 extreme excitement 在程度词 extreme=high、情绪词 excitement=arousal 两个维度上完全对位。

pairs.orig: Their heart rate is elevated ... jump collectively ... emit high-pitched warning calls

option_analysis.note: spiritual elevation 指「精神升华」，原文只描写心率 elevated 这种生理升高，未提及任何精神层面的升华。
intense curiosity 把状态偷换成「强烈好奇」；但原文是因恐怖剧情引发的恐惧式高唤起，不是认知性好奇。

questions.stem: Why do many people seek out scary entertainment, according to the author's research?
questions.stem_zh: 根据作者的研究,为什么许多人会寻求恐怖娱乐?

options.text: They gain experience in overcoming horror in real life.
options.zh: 他们获得了克服现实生活中恐怖的经验。

options.text: They find joy in going through simulated horrible experiences.
options.zh: 他们在经历模拟的恐怖体验中找到乐趣。

options.text: They have learned from hide-and-seek as kids the thrill involved.
options.zh: 他们从儿时的捉迷藏游戏中学到了其中的刺激感。

options.text: They have evolved to gain pleasure in escaping life-threatening situations.
options.zh: 他们进化出了在逃离危及生命的情境中获得快乐的能力。

questions.判型: according to the author's research 把答案限制为作者研究中的一个具体结论，问的是事实层面的原因而非整体主旨，属细节题。
questions.拆句: Q47 主句 Why do many people seek out scary entertainment 是标准 Why 一般疑问句；according to the author's research 是插入语，提示信源限定；seek out 是「主动去寻找」，与原文 voluntarily expose / seek out 同义，注意主动义。
questions.定位: P8 My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. 我的研究表明，人类在进化中学会了在能让我们于安全语境下体验负面情绪的情景中获得快感。

locate.en: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context.
locate.zh: 我的研究表明，人类在进化中学会了在能让我们于安全语境下体验负面情绪的情景中获得快感。

option_analysis.note: They gain experience in overcoming horror in real life 把「安全语境的模拟体验」偷换成「现实生活中克服恐怖」，与原文 safe context 矛盾。
They find joy in going through simulated horrible experiences 两端都吻合预判：joy=pleasure、simulated horrible experiences=negative emotions in a safe context。

pairs.orig: experience negative emotions in a safe context

option_analysis.note: They have learned from hide-and-seek as kids the thrill involved 拿一个例证 hide-and-seek 当原因，又把 pleasure 改成 thrill；hide-and-seek 是论据而非原因，本身不能解释成年人为何看恐怖片。
They have evolved to gain pleasure in escaping life-threatening situations 把「在安全语境下体验负面情绪」偷换成「在逃离致命威胁中获得快感」——原文是模拟、非真威胁；evolved、pleasure 借词制造伪等值。

questions.stem: What do children learn from hide-and-seek?
questions.stem_zh: 孩子们从捉迷藏中学到了什么?

options.text: How to avoid falling prey to an attacker.
options.zh: 如何避免成为攻击者的猎物。

options.text: How to simulate a predator-prey interaction.
options.zh: 如何模拟捕食者与猎物的互动。

options.text: How to keep themselves from catastrophic errors.
options.zh: 如何防止自己犯下灾难性错误。

options.text: How to turn a dangerous scenario into a safe one.
options.zh: 如何将危险场景转变为安全场景。

questions.判型: What do children learn from hide-and-seek 问的是一个可在原文一句话里找到的具体收获，属典型细节题。
questions.拆句: Q48 主干 What do children learn from hide-and-seek 是标准 wh- 疑问；learn from 是「从……中学到」，要求原文有相应的因果或收获句，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P9 This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario. 这种模拟向孩子提供了关于「如何避免成为猎物」的关键信息，孩子往往觉得这种活动极其令人满足，大概是因为它让他们在安全条件下体验了一种潜在的灾难性情境。

locate.en: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
locate.zh: 这种模拟向孩子提供了关于「如何避免成为猎物」的关键信息，孩子往往觉得这种活动极其令人满足，大概是因为它让他们在安全条件下体验了一种潜在的灾难性情境。

option_analysis.note: How to avoid falling prey to an attacker 是预判的近乎逐字改写，avoid 对 avoid、falling prey 对 becoming prey、attacker 对 predator。

pairs.opt: How to avoid falling prey to an attacker

pairs.orig: The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator

option_analysis.note: How to simulate a predator-prey interaction 学的是「如何模拟捕食情境」，但原文说「这场模拟（this simulation）」是大人创造的，孩子从中学到的是避险知识，而不是模拟技巧本身。
How to keep themselves from catastrophic errors 凭空造出「灾难性错误」一说；原文只有 catastrophic scenario「灾难性情境」，且讨论的是体验该情境而非「避免错误」。
How to turn a dangerous scenario into a safe one 把原文「在安全条件下体验潜在的灾难性情境」偷换成「把危险情境变安全」——原文的 safe 是体验时的环境条件，并非孩子把危险情境改造成了安全情境。

questions.stem: Why is horror gratifying to many people?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么恐怖对许多人来说是令人满足的?

options.text: It reminds them of an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms.
options.zh: 它让他们想起一套古老的生物防御机制。

options.text: It triggers their imagination to travel into dangerous virtual worlds.
options.zh: 它激发他们的想象力进入危险的虚拟世界。

options.text: It allows them to learn what fear feels like and how to tackle it.
options.zh: 它让他们学习恐惧的感觉以及如何应对恐惧。

options.text: It activates their evolved fear system and their unique fantasy.
options.zh: 它激活了他们进化而来的恐惧系统和独特的幻想能力。

questions.判型: Why is horror gratifying to many people 问的是可在一句原文中找到的因果细节，作者给出明确的 because 句，非整体主旨。
questions.拆句: Q49 主干 Why is horror gratifying to many people 是 be + adj. 的因果疑问句；gratifying 是现在分词作表语，等同 pleasing，要在原文找其同义表达 pleasurable，无结构陷阱。
questions.定位: P11 Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion. 对许多人而言，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们演练负面情绪并发展出应对策略。我们由此了解真正害怕的感觉，也学会如何处理负面情绪。

locate.en: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
locate.zh: 对许多人而言，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们演练负面情绪并发展出应对策略。我们由此了解真正害怕的感觉，也学会如何处理负面情绪。

option_analysis.note: It reminds them of an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms 把「让我们演练负面情绪」偷换成「让我们想起远古防御机制」——原文是「利用」(exploiting) 防御机制，而不是「使我们回忆起」。
It triggers their imagination to travel into dangerous virtual worlds 描述的是恐怖如何作用（机制），而非「为什么令人满足」（原因）；机制 vs 原因不同问，且 P12 的话题是 how，不是 why。
learn what fear feels like and how to tackle it 用并列结构同时覆盖预判的两层「体验」和「应对」，是原文最完整的同义改写。

pairs.orig: We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid
develop coping strategies ... learn how to handle negative emotion

option_analysis.note: It activates their evolved fear system and their unique fantasy 是把 P12 机制段的两个核心要素「evolved fear system」与「imagination」拼起来，依旧回答的是「机制」而非「为什么令人满足」。

questions.stem: What will one experience if they watch a horror film through without being hurt?
questions.stem_zh: 如果一个人毫发无损地看完一部恐怖电影,他们会体验到什么?

options.text: A strong sense of clear relevance.
options.zh: 强烈的明确相关感。

options.text: A profound sense of good fortune.
options.zh: 深刻的幸运感。

options.text: A profound sense of intense relief.
options.zh: 深刻的强烈解脱感。

options.text: A strong sense of being in control.
options.zh: 强烈的掌控感。

questions.判型: What will one experience 询问的是一段可被定位的具体心理体验，原文末段以 you'll probably experience 直接给出，按细节题处理。
questions.拆句: Q50 主干 What will one experience 是宾语前置的 wh- 疑问；if they watch a horror film through without being hurt 是条件状语从句，through 是副词「自始至终」，without being hurt 是被动动名词作伴随状语；they 指代 one，无指代陷阱。
questions.定位: P13 If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. 如果你能毫发无损地撑过这部电影，你大概会体验到一种强烈的掌控感——一种自己能挺过令人毛骨悚然之体验的胜任感。

locate.en: If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.
locate.zh: 如果你能毫发无损地撑过这部电影，你大概会体验到一种强烈的掌控感——一种自己能挺过令人毛骨悚然之体验的胜任感。

option_analysis.note: A strong sense of clear relevance 摘取原文末句 critically relevant 中 relevant 的衍生形态，把后置的 critically relevant 偷换为 clear relevance；原文是说「处理恐惧的能力未来可能会变得至关重要」，并非「看完后体验到清晰的相关感」。
A profound sense of good fortune 描述「幸运感」，原文从未提及；作者强调的是因撑过而获得的胜任感，而非「庆幸自己运气好」。
A profound sense of intense relief 描述「释然感」，原文没有任何「relief/放松」语义；mastery 强调的是控场，而非紧张消退。
strong sense of 对原文原词，mastery 与 being in control 是同义场最佳对应，D 字面命中预判。

pairs.opt: A strong sense of being in control

pairs.orig: a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience

reading2.title: 2024年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
passages.zh: 在现实世界中，一场反对多年来强加给我们的美丽标准的觉醒正在发生。然而，在数字领域，社交媒体决定着什么才被视为美丽。

passages.en: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate". At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
passages.zh: 这两种相互对立的斗争正在并行展开。在现实世界中，这场斗争反对的是施加在女性身上的、要求她们符合不切实际的美丽理想的潜在压力。作为这场斗争的一部分，各种媒体纷纷呈现身材不符合所谓理想标准的女性。所有那些过去被排除在杂志封面、电视连续剧和公共议题之外的女性，如今都变得“名正言顺”了。与此同时，一群有影响力的人开始在社交媒体上上传自己不化妆的照片，甚至上传突出所谓缺陷的照片。

passages.en: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look", which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
passages.zh: 科技重塑了我们的美丽理想，并且非常有效地将这一信息传递给大众。过去十年留下的奇怪遗产之一，就是“赛博格外貌”的流行；这种外貌展现了美国人在2050年可能呈现的样子。

passages.en: The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
passages.zh: 赛博格外貌迅速传播开来。然而，如今Instagram脸已经成为新的美丽理想。

passages.en: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified(游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
passages.zh: 当人们积极参与学习过程时，对公认美丽规范的内化会更加有效。用户的积极参与体现在社交媒体平台所提供的游戏化互动中，即点赞、发表评论、比较和分享的能力。

passages.en: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
passages.zh: 一旦人们内化了理想的美丽标准，用户就会获得各种工具或功能，用来改变自己的外貌，使其符合公认的美丽标准，例如编辑图像、选择理想的滤镜和合适的背景。

passages.en: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
passages.zh: 一项在美国开展的调查显示，超过50%的人会在发布图像前对其进行滤镜处理。听到其中大多数是女性，你不会感到惊讶。过度使用滤镜的一个重要后果，是人们越来越倾向于把自己当作一个供人观察和评价的对象，就像另一个人从旁观察和评判自己一样。

passages.en: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
passages.zh: 滤镜所产生的影响已经远远超出了友善的消遣范畴。滤镜以及网络上进行的整个游戏都会影响用户的心理健康。一项研究表明，Instagram、Snapchat和FaceTune等应用程序能让用户达到一种此前只有在美容杂志中才能看到的完美程度。

passages.en: Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.
passages.zh: 尽管人类一直珍视美丽，但在过去十年里，我们对外表的痴迷已经达到前所未有的高峰。花在社交媒体上的时间催生出一种强烈的冲动，促使人们追求不可能实现的美丽理想；唯一能够解决这一问题的，不是整容干预，而是心理健康护理。

questions.stem: What do we learn about beauty in the digital arena?
questions.stem_zh: 关于数字领域的美,我们了解到什么?

options.text: It dictates the taste of digital media.
options.zh: 它主宰着数字媒体的品味。

options.text: It has been in the making for years.
options.zh: 它已经酝酿多年。

options.text: It has ushered in a new awakening.
options.zh: 它开启了一种新的觉醒。

options.text: It is defined by social media.
options.zh: 它由社交媒体定义。

questions.判型: 题干 What do we learn about beauty in the digital arena 是问"关于 X 我们了解到什么",指向原文对 X 的客观陈述。
questions.拆句: Q51 是一个简单的 wh-疑问句,主干 What do we learn (about X),about 短语作 learn 的状语,整句无从句、无否定,无理解陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful. 但在数字领域,是社交媒体决定了什么才被认为是美的。

locate.en: But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
locate.zh: 但在数字领域,是社交媒体决定了什么才被认为是美的。

option_analysis.note: It dictates the taste of digital media 让"美"反过来去 dictate digital media,原文是 social media 在 determine beauty,主客被掉换。
It has been in the making for years 谈的是"已经酝酿多年",原文只说 dictated to us for years 的是"physical world 的旧美标准",并非 beauty in the digital arena 本身。
It has ushered in a new awakening 说"数字领域的美开启了新觉醒",但原文 An awakening has been taking place in the physical world 明确把觉醒放在 physical world,而非 digital arena。
It is defined by social media 几乎就是预判句"美由社交媒体决定"的英文被动版,正中定位句 social media determines what is considered beautiful 的核心信息。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about beauty in the physical world?
questions.stem_zh: 文章关于现实世界中的美说了什么?

options.text: Women are under constant pressure to keep up with beauty models.
options.zh: 女性承受着持续的压力以跟上美的模板。

options.text: Women are encouraged to pursue a beauty ideal that has never existed.
options.zh: 女性被鼓励追求一种从未存在过的美的理想。

options.text: A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal.
options.zh: 一场斗争正在进行,旨在消除女性顺应荒谬美的理想的压力。

options.text: Media outlets have begun to present as beauty models trendy women without any makeup.
options.zh: 媒体机构已开始将不化妆的时尚女性作为美的模板呈现。

questions.判型: What does the passage say about beauty in the physical world 直接问"文章对 X 怎么说",取的是原文事实陈述。
questions.拆句: Q52 主干 What does the passage say (about X),about 短语后置作 say 的状语,无从句、无否定,理解无障碍。
questions.定位: P2 In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. 在现实世界里,这场斗争所反对的是施加在女性身上、要求她们顺从一种不切实际的美标准的潜在压力。

locate.en: In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal.

option_analysis.note: Women are under constant pressure to keep up with beauty models 强调女性"持续被施压",方向恰好与原文的"对抗这种压力"相反,文章重点在抗争,而非顺从。
Women are encouraged to pursue a beauty ideal that has never existed 中的 encouraged to pursue 在原文找不到对应——原文谈的是被施压,而非被鼓励;"never existed"也并非原文 unrealistic 的等值表达。
A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal 把"正在进行抗争"+"对象是施加在女性身上的、要她们顺从荒谬美标准的压力"两层全保留,正是预判内容。

pairs.opt: A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal

questions.判型: What do we learn from the passage about the Instagram face 仍是问对 X 这一具体对象的客观陈述。
questions.拆句: Q53 主干 What do we learn (from the passage) (about X),两个介词短语都作状语,无从句、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal. 然而,如今 Instagram face 已经成为新的美标准。

locate.en: Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.

option_analysis.note: It is what most women will go after in 2050 把"2050"这个时间安在 Instagram face 头上,而 the popularity of the cyborg look, which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050 里 2050 描述的是 cyborg look,而非 Instagram face。
It is being much talked about on social media 加入了"正在被大量讨论"这层意思,原文只说它"成了新美标准",并未提及讨论度。
